name: quit-palette-open
description: Matrix A. Identical to empty-window-quit except the auto-opened command palette is NOT dismissed - the palette window owns key focus when Cmd+Q arrives. AtriumCommandBarDispatcherDelegate declines the chord in prePerform (Cmd+Q is not in NativeHotkeyMap) and routes it to the main menu in postPerform; this asserts that route actually quits.

actions.note: let the empty space render; the palette auto-opens when there is no restored tab, and is deliberately left up. 8000 not 4000: the palette appears 3.9-5.0s after launch on this VM, so the old value raced it and the run could reach Cmd+Q with no palette at all - the premise silently absent. The palette-had-key gate below now catches that, but not racing it in the first place is better
evidence of the exact state Cmd+Q is pressed in

assertions.label: palette-had-key
assertions.note: Gate on the PREMISE: this scenario is about the palette route, so the palette must actually be up and focused when Cmd+Q lands. Pre-quit line, so it is checked against the pre-quit log.

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q quits while the command palette holds key focus (palette postPerform -> main menu route)

assertions.label: palette-route-taken
assertions.pattern: Atrium: palette passing key-equivalent to main menu
assertions.note: Listed AFTER the quit assertion on purpose: the run log is pulled before assertions run, so a line Cmd+Q itself emits is only in the log that assert_quit re-pulls. Placed before it, this gate could never match - and a vlog_absent one would pass trivially, which is exactly the vacuous shape to avoid.
